name: Reinterpretation (taʾwīl)
definition: Reading a usage that seems to break a rule in a way that brings it back under the rule: by supplying a hidden word, by another iʿrāb, or by another sense.
body: When a verse or a saying goes against a rule, the grammarian has three answers: call it shādhdh, call it a licence of verse (ḍarūra), or interpret it (taʾwīl). The Basrans used taʾwīl much more than the Kufans, who would rather make a new rule from the usage; in al-Inṣāf most of Ibn al-Anbārī's answers for Basra are taʾwīls of the Kufans' evidence. The commentaries mark it with 'it is to be interpreted as…' (muʾawwal bi-…) or 'on the assumption of…' (ʿalā taqdīr…).
